brief: Stat of the day: hedge funds net sold global Energy at the fastest pace in four months, split roughly evenly between shorts and longs, while retail keeps buying even as HF net/gross exposure and sentiment sit near lows. Rates: the Fed's inflation focus should extend near-term curve flattening because steepening needs clarity on how many hikes remain, so GS prefers selling vol on longer tenors over duration and holds long EUR 1y1y vs CHF since a hawkish ECB energy reaction function protects belly forwards. The BoE's Gilt-friendly QT bull-flattened the UK curve and points to a November hike, keeping gaps like M7M8 flattening; the BoJ's 25bp hike undershot hawkish expectations, so GS favors paying 5y JPY on the 2s5s10s fly. MSFT NDR: front-loaded capex and balanced 1P/3P and frontier/enterprise allocation drove all of 4Q's $51bn RPO increase from enterprises, cutting reliance on any one model (Buy, Conviction List). Solar: weak resi demand plus rate headwinds mean a subdued recovery into 1Q27 (ENPH Buy, RUN Buy despite a rate-driven valuation headwind, SEDG Sell). Market close: Anthropic's Dario Doomsday call for slower AI progress drove GS's AI-vs-AI-at-risk pair to its worst day since DeepSeek as the 10yr backed toward 5%, while oil sold off and East-West pipeline talks turned positive ahead of the UN General Assembly. YETI set FY30 growth and FCF targets at its investor day.
